title: Maps

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Maps** as part of **Strings, Arrays, and Collections**. A map stores values associated with keys; key uniqueness, missing-key handling, and the chosen mutable/read-only API affect design. Use the subtopics—Keys and Values, Accessing and Updating Map Entries, Map Construction and Transformation—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Functions, null safety, strings, and collections are the building blocks of most practical Kotlin code. Choosing the right operation reduces avoidable errors and makes behavior easier to test.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: A read-only collection reference proves that no code can mutate the underlying data.
